pr_comments: I find `is_first` and `is_last` rather non-descript names. Maybe `is_first_occurrence`? Or `is_first_distinct`?

> I find is_first and is_last rather non-descript names. Maybe is_first_occurrence? Or is_first_distinct?

Totally agree with you, and I was also initially confused by this name. I will open an issue to solicit everyone's opinions.

> I find `is_first` and `is_last` rather non-descript names. Maybe `is_first_occurrence`? Or `is_first_distinct`?

`is_last_distinct` sounds good to me. Though we use `unique` instead of `distinct` everywhere else. So maybe `is_last_unique`?

@stinodego `unique`ness is a post-condition in the other cases. I don't think it's appropriate here, because we're not returning unique values, nor are the places we in the mask corresponding to unique values. Also, the "last unique value" reads very weird because a unique value.. is the only value.

~~As another possibility, we could do `is_first_by`, which indicates that a row is the first value in its group when grouped by the given column.~~ Never mind didn't realize this is a method on a series, not an expression.

> @orlp has some good points about the suboptimal design of our current is_first. Maybe we should first fix/improve those, so we can reuse some of that new architecture in this PR.

@ritchie46, will @orlp open a new PR specifically to handle this optimazation? If so, I will rebase and refactor this PR based on his excellent work. If not, I may continue to rewrite `is_last` for boolean type alone with his comment. Both are good for me, so it's up to you. ^ ^

issue_context.title: `is_last()`
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

To go with [`.is_first()`](https://pola-rs.github.io/polars/py-polars/html/reference/expressions/api/polars.Expr.is_first.html)

There does seem to be mention of `is_last` already in the codebase:

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/polars/src/lib.rs#L224

```rust
//!     - `is_last` - Check if element is last unique value.
```

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/polars/polars-core/src/chunked_array/ops/mod.rs#L757

But it doesn't seem to exist?
comments:
I guess it can be emulated by checking counts with `.over()`
```python
pl.Expr.is_last = lambda expr: (
   pl.int_range(0, pl.count()) ==
   pl.int_range(0, pl.count()).max()
).over(expr)

```
I believe we already have this? Did we not expose this?

Perhaps I'm being `.rank("dense")` - but there doesn't seem to be an implementation of it.

There's no `is_last.rs` in polars-ops

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/polars/polars-ops/src/series/ops/

(I'm guessing that's where it would be as that is where `is_first.rs` lives)
@ritchie46 there's a trait defined for it, and it's listed as an operation in `Cargo.toml` but there's no implementation anywhere.

review_comments:
Can we directly set the bits on a `Vec<u8>` here? That would save us going from `Vec<bool>` which a a byte per boolean and then copying that into the bitmaks of a bit per boolean.

I believe we already do this correctly in the code below.

Initially, I impl this based on `downcast_iter + arr.into_iter`. But that way requires us to collect both the inner and outer iterator in reverse order. For the inner loop, I just introduce `impl FromIteratorReversed<bool> for BooleanArray`. But for the outer loop, we also need to make `ChunkedArray::from_chunk_iter` supports reverse collection, but I'm not sure if this is suitable, so I have changed to the non nested loop approach.

Maybe we can rechunk and then iterate over the arrow array.

This should make iteration fast for the most common case.
Here we need to be able to get the reverse slicing of `Bitmap`. I haven't found the corresponding API. Does anyone know about this or other better ways of fast path.
I think this now becomes redundant with: `find_first_true_false_no_null`, or at least part of that implementation can be reused here.
I don't like this implementation, I think it could be a lot faster using `[u8]::align_to::<u64>`. Could be even faster with SIMD.

This two method is just moved from `arg_min_max.rs`, I didn't delve into the details of code.
